name: 8651-shortprompt-7b-1gpu
hardware: 1x H100 80GB HBM3 (one GPU of an a3 node, --gres=gpu:1), SM90, CUDA 12.x
parallelism: TP=1, PP=1, DP=1, one in-process vLLM engine
load_profile: concurrent (CLOSED loop), streams=1024 against a 256-slot engine so the waiting queue stays deep, bounded at 40000 requests / 900 s safety, warmup the first 25% by completion.
workload: guidellm `synthetic_text`, single turn, no prefix_buckets, prompt exactly 35 tokens and output exactly 35 (min = max = 35 on both), `request_format: plain`.
purpose: A 7-billion-parameter chat assistant giving brief replies to one-line questions for over a thousand simultaneous users on a single GPU.
launch:
# The engine's command line at commit cd9d06fb8d1f89fc1bcc9305bc20d57c6d8b73d8.
# Interpreter and hardware seal live in configs/env.yaml, which is per-machine and NOT portable.
#
# 0.6.6-era AsyncEngineArgs: an unknown key is a TypeError at engine construction, so do not add
# keys from a later vLLM.

model: NousResearch/Llama-2-7b-hf

# The checkpoint on disk is fp16; this flag quantizes the linear weights at load time.
quantization: fp8

tensor-parallel-size: 1
dtype: float16
max-num-seqs: 256
max-num-batched-tokens: 4096
gpu-memory-utilization: 0.90

# The synthetic workload has no shared prefix, so caching has nothing to hit; pinned off.
enable-prefix-caching: false

# Eager: the declared operating point, and the one the source's own absolute numbers look like
# (152.6 req/s at 70 tok/req on an H100 is below an eager run on this machine, not above a
# captured one).
#
# It is not a workaround: on the v0.6.6 wheel, whose bindings match the pin, CUDA-graph capture
# completes in 11 s over all 35 shapes. A v0.7.3 wheel is what fails: its _C.abi3.so declares
# reshape_and_cache_flash(..., Tensor k_scale) against a checkout that passes a float, so every
# request dies, capture never advances past its first shape and the engine rebuilds in a loop
# until the run is killed for host memory.
enforce-eager: true
